<result>///
/// Functions that take data return [`MusicError`] for data they cannot use (wrong row
/// count, no samples, NaN, silence) and for invalid parameters (too many sources, an
/// unusable STFT size or bin list).
///
/// # Examples
/// ```
/// use musicrs::MusicEstimator;
/// let est = MusicEstimator::default(); // Kinect 4-mic array, 720 angle steps, [0, 2π)
/// ```
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct MusicEstimator {
    /// Antenna (microphone) positions as `[x, y]` pairs in metres.
    pub antenna_positions: Vec<[f64; 2]>,
    /// Number of angle steps in the angular search grid.
    pub angle_steps_num: usize,
    /// Angular search range `(start_rad, end_rad)`; the grid includes `start_rad` and
    /// excludes `end_rad`. A range spanning exactly 2π is treated as the full circle (its
    /// ends are adjacent when picking peaks); any other range is open at both ends.
    pub search_interval: (f64, f64),
    /// Sample rate of the input signal in Hz, used to determine the sign convention
    /// for the steering vector (positive exponent for f < sr/2, negative for f ≥ sr/2).
    pub sample_rate: f64,
}

impl Default for MusicEstimator {
    /// Returns an estimator configured for the 4-element Kinect microphone array
    /// with 720 angle steps over the full circle [0, 2π).
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            antenna_positions: DEFAULT_ANTENNA_POSITIONS.to_vec(),
            angle_steps_num: 720,
            search_interval: (0.0, 2.0 * PI),
            sample_rate: 16000.0,
        }
    }
}

impl MusicEstimator {
    /// Creates a new `MusicEstimator`.
    ///
    /// # Arguments
    /// * `antenna_positions` – Slice of `[x, y]` positions in metres.
    /// * `angle_steps_num`   – Number of discrete angles to evaluate.
    /// * `search_interval`   – `(start_rad, end_rad)` search range.
    /// * `sample_rate`       – Sample rate in Hz (used for aliasing-aware steering).
    ///
    /// Nothing is checked here, because the fields are public and can change later. The
    /// methods that use them return [`MusicError::InvalidAngleGrid`] unless
    /// `angle_steps_num > 0` and `search_interval` is finite with `start < end` and spans
    /// at most 2π, [`MusicError::InvalidSampleRate`] unless `sample_rate` is finite and
    /// positive, and [`MusicError::InvalidAntennaPosition`] for a NaN or infinite position.
    pub fn new(
        antenna_positions: Vec<[f64; 2]>,
        angle_steps_num: usize,
        search_interval: (f64, f64),
        sample_rate: f64,
    ) -> Self {
        Self {
            antenna_positions,
            angle_steps_num,
            search_interval,
            sample_rate,
        }
    }

    /// Number of antennas in the array.
    #[inline]
    pub fn n_antennas(&self) -> usize {
        self.antenna_positions.len()
    }

    /// Whether [`search_interval`](Self::search_interval) spans exactly the full circle,
    /// so that the first and last grid angles are neighbours.
    fn covers_full_circle(&self) -> bool {
        let (start, end) = self.search_interval;
        ((end - start).abs() - 2.0 * PI).abs() <= 1e-9
    }

    /// The search grid: `angle_steps_num` angles from `start` (included) to `end`
    /// (excluded). pyMUSIC asserts `start < end` in `MUSICEst.__init__`.
    fn angle_grid(&self) -> Result<Vec<f64>> {
        let (start, end) = self.search_interval;
        let steps = self.angle_steps_num;
        let usable = start.is_finite() && end.is_finite() && start < end;
        // A span of more than 2π (beyond the tolerance of `covers_full_circle`) would
        // visit some directions twice and report one source as two.
        if steps == 0 || !usable || end - start > 2.0 * PI + 1e-9 {
            return Err(MusicError::InvalidAngleGrid {
                angle_steps_num: steps,
                search_interval: self.search_interval,
            });
        }
        Ok((0..steps)
            .map(|i| start + (end - start) * i as f64 / steps as f64)
            .collect())
    }

    /// Checks the fields the steering vectors are built from: a finite, positive
    /// `sample_rate` and finite antenna positions.
    fn check_array(&self) -> Result<()> {
        if !(self.sample_rate.is_finite() && self.sample_rate > 0.0) {
            return Err(MusicError::InvalidSampleRate(self.sample_rate));
        }
        match self
            .antenna_positions
            .iter()
            .position(|p| !(p[0].is_finite() && p[1].is_finite()))
        {
            Some(index) => Err(MusicError::InvalidAntennaPosition { index }),
            None => Ok(()),
        }
    }

    fn check_rows(&self, got: usize) -> Result<()> {
        if got == self.n_antennas() {
            Ok(())
        } else {
            Err(MusicError::RowCountMismatch {
                expected: self.n_antennas(),
                got,
            })
        }
    }

    /// Checks that a signal frequency is finite and positive.
    fn check_frequency(frequency: f64) -> Result<()> {
        if frequency.is_finite() && frequency > 0.0 {
            Ok(())
        } else {
            Err(MusicError::InvalidFrequency(frequency))
        }
    }

    /// Checks that `0 < n_sources < n_antennas`. Zero sources would make the noise
    /// subspace the whole space and the spectrum meaningless.
    fn check_sources(&self, n_sources: usize) -> Result<()> {
        if n_sources >= self.n_antennas() {
            Err(MusicError::TooManySources {
                n_sources,
                n_antennas: self.n_antennas(),
            })
        } else if n_sources == 0 {
            Err(MusicError::NoSources)
        } else {
            Ok(())
        }
    }

    // ─── Core algorithm ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    /// Computes the steering vector for a plane wave arriving from `angle` (radians)
    /// at `frequency` (Hz).
    ///
    /// Element *j* is `exp(+i·2π·f·τⱼ)` where `τⱼ = (pⱼ · d̂) / c` is the projection of
    /// antenna *j*'s position onto the arrival direction, divided by the speed of sound. This
    /// matches the non-conjugated [`analytic_signal`] and STFT bins
    /// (pyMUSIC conjugates its analytic signal and uses `exp(−i·2π·f·τⱼ)`; the two agree below
    /// Nyquist). Relative to [`sample_rate`](Self::sample_rate):
    /// * above Nyquist the exponent is negated, `exp(−i·2π·f·τⱼ)`, because the recorded tone
    ///   is aliased and its phase is conjugated;
    /// * within 0.5 Hz of Nyquist the vector is real, `cos(2π·f·τⱼ)`, because the analytic
    ///   signal there is real too.
    ///
    /// # Examples
    /// ```
    /// use musicrs::MusicEstimator;
    /// let est = MusicEstimator::default();
    /// let sv = est.steering_vector(0.0, 300.0);
    /// assert_eq!(sv.len(), 4);
    /// // All elements have unit magnitude
    /// for c in sv.iter() {
    ///     assert!((c.norm() - 1.0).abs() < 1e-12);
    /// }
    /// ```
    pub fn steering_vector(&self, angle: f64, frequency: f64) -> CVec {
        let mut out = vec![Cplx::new(0.0, 0.0); self.n_antennas()];
        self.steering_vector_into(angle, frequency, &mut out);
        CVec::from_vec(out)
    }

    /// [`steering_vector`](Self::steering_vector) written into `out` (one element per
    /// antenna), so that the spectrum does not allocate a vector per angle.
    fn steering_vector_into(&self, angle: f64, frequency: f64, out: &mut [Cplx]) {
        let dir = [angle.cos(), angle.sin()];
        // For f < Nyquist (sr/2): analytic signal has positive phase → use +exponent.
        // For f > Nyquist: signal aliases in the one-sided FFT; dominant eigenvector
        // phase is conjugated → use −exponent.
        // At exactly Nyquist (f == sr/2): analytic signal is real; noise subspace is
        // also real → use cos(phase) as a real steering vector.
        let nyquist = self.sample_rate / 2.0;
        let phase_sign = if frequency > nyquist {
            -1.0_f64
        } else {
            1.0_f64
        };
        let at_nyquist = (frequency - nyquist).abs() < 0.5;
        for (element, p) in out.iter_mut().zip(&self.antenna_positions) {
            let delay = (p[0] * dir[0] + p[1] * dir[1]) / SPEED_OF_SOUND;
            let phase = phase_sign * 2.0 * PI * frequency * delay;
            *element = if at_nyquist {
                // Real steering vector: imaginary part is zero
                Cplx::new(phase.cos(), 0.0)
            } else {
                Cplx::from_polar(1.0, phase)
            };
        }
    }

    /// Extracts the noise subspace from the Hermitian covariance matrix `cov`.
    ///
    /// Eigendecomposes `cov`, sorts eigenvectors by ascending eigenvalue magnitude,
    /// and returns the `n − n_sources` columns spanning the noise subspace.
    ///
    /// # Arguments
    /// * `cov`       – Hermitian covariance matrix (n_antennas × n_antennas).
    /// * `n_sources` – Number of signal sources (must be in `1..n_antennas`).
    ///
    /// `cov` is assumed to be Hermitian, as every covariance matrix is: only its lower
    /// triangle (diagonal included) is read.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// [`MusicError::CovarianceShape`] if `cov` is not n_antennas × n_antennas,
    /// [`MusicError::NonFiniteData`] if it contains NaN or infinity,
    /// [`MusicError::TooManySources`] if `n_sources >= n_antennas`, and
    /// [`MusicError::NoSources`] if `n_sources` is 0.
    pub fn noise_subspace(&self, cov: &CMatrix, n_sources: usize) -> Result<CMatrix> {
        let n = self.n_antennas();
        if cov.shape() != (n, n) {
            return Err(MusicError::CovarianceShape {
                n_antennas: n,
                rows: cov.nrows(),
                cols: cov.ncols(),
            });
        }
        self.check_sources(n_sources)?;
        if !cov.iter().all(|c| c.re.is_finite() && c.im.is_finite()) {
            return Err(MusicError::NonFiniteData);
        }

        // Eigenvectors in ascending eigenvalue order; the first n_noise columns are the
        // noise subspace (smallest eigenvalues).
        let (_eigenvalues, eigenvectors) = hermitian_eigen(cov);
        let n_noise = cov.nrows() - n_sources;
        Ok(eigenvectors.columns(0, n_noise).into())
    }

    /// Generates the MUSIC pseudo-spectrum.
    ///
    /// For each angle θ in the search grid, the score is `1 / ‖Eₙᴴ · a(θ)‖²`.
    /// High values indicate signal directions of arrival.
    ///
    /// # Arguments
    /// * `noise_mat` – Noise subspace matrix (n_antennas × n_noise) from
    ///   [`noise_subspace`](Self::noise_subspace).
    /// * `frequency` – Signal frequency in Hz.
    ///
    /// # Returns
    /// `(spectrum, angles)` — corresponding vectors of the same length.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// - [`MusicError::RowCountMismatch`] if `noise_mat` does not have one row per antenna.
    /// - [`MusicError::InvalidFrequency`] unless `frequency` is finite and positive.
    /// - [`MusicError::InvalidAngleGrid`], [`MusicError::InvalidSampleRate`] or
    ///   [`MusicError::InvalidAntennaPosition`] for an unusable estimator (see [`new`](Self::new)).
    pub fn spectrum(&self, noise_mat: &CMatrix, frequency: f64) -> Result<(Vec<f64>, Vec<f64>)> {
        self.check_rows(noise_mat.nrows())?;
        self.check_array()?;
        Self::check_frequency(frequency)?;
        let angles = self.angle_grid()?;
        let mut a = vec![Cplx::new(0.0, 0.0); self.n_antennas()];
        let scores: Vec<f64> = angles
            .iter()
            .map(|&theta| {
                self.steering_vector_into(theta, frequency, &mut a);
                // ‖Eₙᴴ a‖²: one inner product per noise eigenvector (column of noise_mat)
                let denom: f64 = noise_mat
                    .column_iter()
                    .map(|e| {
                        e.iter()
                            .zip(&a)
                            .map(|(e, a)| e.conj() * a)
                            .sum::<Cplx>()
                            .norm_sqr()
                    })
                    .sum();
                if denom == 0.0 {
                    f64::INFINITY
                } else {
                    1.0 / denom
                }
            })
            .collect();

        Ok((scores, angles))
    }

    /// Estimates the directions of arrival for `n_sources` narrowband sources.
    ///
    /// # Arguments
    /// * `data`      – Complex array data (n_antennas × n_samples).
    /// * `n_sources` – Number of sources to detect.
    /// * `frequency` – Signal frequency in Hz.
    ///
    /// # Returns
    /// Up to `n_sources` estimated angles (radians), sorted by descending peak height.
    ///
    /// The sources must be uncorrelated. Coherent sources (the same tone from two
    /// directions with a fixed phase relation, such as two loudspeakers on one signal or a
    /// reflection) give a covariance of rank 1, like a single source, and the estimates
    /// point in neither direction.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// - [`MusicError::RowCountMismatch`] if `data` does not have one row per antenna.
    /// - [`MusicError::EmptyData`] if it has no samples, [`MusicError::NonFiniteData`]
    ///   if it contains NaN or infinity, [`MusicError::SilentData`] if it is all zeros.
    /// - [`MusicError::TooManySources`] if `n_sources >= n_antennas`, [`MusicError::NoSources`]
    ///   if it is 0.
    /// - [`MusicError::InvalidFrequency`] unless `frequency` is finite and positive.
    /// - [`MusicError::InvalidAngleGrid`], [`MusicError::InvalidSampleRate`] or
    ///   [`MusicError::InvalidAntennaPosition`] for an unusable estimator (see [`new`](Self::new)).
    pub fn estimate_doa(
        &self,
        data: &CMatrix,
        n_sources: usize,
        frequency: f64,
    ) -> Result<Vec<f64>> {
        self.check_rows(data.nrows())?;
        self.check_sources(n_sources)?;
        self.check_array()?;
        Self::check_frequency(frequency)?;
        if data.ncols() == 0 {
            return Err(MusicError::EmptyData);
        }
        if !data.iter().all(|c| c.re.is_finite() && c.im.is_finite()) {
            return Err(MusicError::NonFiniteData);
        }
        let max_abs = data
            .iter()
            .fold(0.0, |m: f64, c| m.max(c.re.abs()).max(c.im.abs()));
        let scale = power_of_two_scale(max_abs);
        let data = data.map(|c| c / scale);
        let n_samples = data.ncols() as f64;
        let cov = (&data * data.adjoint()).scale(1.0 / n_samples);
        self.doa_from_covariance(&cov, n_sources, frequency)
    }

    /// The DOA estimates of `estimate_doa` from the covariance `cov` of the array data.
    fn doa_from_covariance(
        &self,
        cov: &CMatrix,
        n_sources: usize,
        frequency: f64,
    ) -> Result<Vec<f64>> {
        if cov.trace().re == 0.0 {
            return Err(MusicError::SilentData);
        }
        let noise_mat = self.noise_subspace(cov, n_sources)?;
        let (scores, angles) = self.spectrum(&noise_mat, frequency)?;
        Ok(find_peaks(
            &scores,
            &angles,
            n_sources,
            self.covers_full_circle(),
        ))
    }

    /// Estimates DOAs from real-valued microphone data, like pyMUSIC's `getSourceAngles`.
    ///
    /// Removes each channel's mean and estimates the DOAs from the covariance of the
    /// channels' analytic signals (as [`analytic_signal`] gives them), with the same
    /// eigendecomposition, spectrum and peak search as [`estimate_doa`](Self::estimate_doa).
    /// Without the mean removal a DC offset acts as a second source at broadside.
    ///
    /// The analytic signals are never formed, and `estimate_doa` is not called: the
    /// covariance is computed directly from the real FFT of each channel (by Parseval's
    /// theorem), which gives the same covariance up to rounding at a fraction of the cost.
    /// The data is scaled by a power of two before that, which is exact, so the covariance
    /// is not rescaled again as `estimate_doa` does with complex data.
    ///
    /// # Arguments
    /// * `data`      – Real array data (n_antennas × n_samples).
    /// * `n_sources` – Number of sources to detect.
    /// * `frequency` – Signal frequency in Hz.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// As [`estimate_doa`](Self::estimate_doa); data that is constant on every channel (its
    /// energy after removing the mean is 260 dB below the input's) is
    /// [`MusicError::SilentData`].
    ///
    /// # Examples
    /// ```
    /// use musicrs::MusicEstimator;
    /// use nalgebra::DMatrix;
    /// use std::f64::consts::PI;
    ///
    /// let est = MusicEstimator::default();
    /// let (freq, doa, sr) = (1000.0, 60.0_f64.to_radians(), est.sample_rate);
    /// // Plane wave: microphone j hears the source delayed by -(p_j · d) / c
    /// let data = DMatrix::from_fn(4, 4000, |j, t| {
    ///     let p = est.antenna_positions[j];
    ///     let advance = (p[0] * doa.cos() + p[1] * doa.sin()) / 343.2;
    ///     (2.0 * PI * freq * (t as f64 / sr + advance)).cos()
    /// });
    /// let angles = est.estimate_doa_from_real(&data, 1, freq)?;
    /// // A linear array cannot tell θ from 360° − θ
    /// let deg = angles[0].to_degrees();
    /// assert!((deg - 60.0).abs() < 2.0 || (deg - 300.0).abs() < 2.0, "got {deg}");
    /// # Ok::<(), musicrs::MusicError>(())
    /// ```
    pub fn estimate_doa_from_real(
        &self,
        data: &DMatrix<f64>,
        n_sources: usize,
        frequency: f64,
    ) -> Result<Vec<f64>> {
        self.check_rows(data.nrows())?;
        self.check_sources(n_sources)?;
        self.check_array()?;
        Self::check_frequency(frequency)?;
        let max_abs = check_real_samples(data)?;
        let mut rows = scaled_rows(data, max_abs);
        let (mut raw_energy, mut centred_energy) = (0.0, 0.0);
        for row in &mut rows {
            let mean = accurate_mean(row.iter());
            for x in row.iter_mut() {
                raw_energy += *x * *x;
                *x -= mean;
                centred_energy += *x * *x;
            }
        }
        if centred_energy <= SILENCE_RATIO * raw_energy {
            return Err(MusicError::SilentData);
        }
        let cov = analytic_covariance(&mut rows);
        self.doa_from_covariance(&cov, n_sources, frequency)
    }

    /// Integrated Frequency-Band (IFB) MUSIC spectrum.
    ///
    /// Computes a narrowband MUSIC spectrum at each frequency bin and combines them
    /// via geometric mean for improved wideband robustness.
    ///
    /// # Arguments
    /// * `data`          – Real-valued microphone data (n_antennas × n_samples).
    /// * `nfft`          – STFT window size.
    /// * `n_sources`     – Number of sources.
    /// * `bins`          – Frequency bin indices to use; `None` uses all bins except DC.
    ///   The DC bin 0 (it has no direction information), bins at or above `nfft / 2 + 1`
    ///   and bins with no power are ignored. Each bin counts once in the geometric mean,
    ///   however often it is listed and in whatever order.
    ///
    /// Bin frequencies are derived from [`MusicEstimator::sample_rate`], the same rate
    /// [`steering_vector`](Self::steering_vector) uses for its Nyquist handling.
    /// Bins only cover `[0, sample_rate / 2]`, so a tone recorded above Nyquist is
    /// steered at its aliased frequency and its DOA cannot be recovered here.
    ///
    /// # Returns
    /// `(spectrum, angles)` — the IFB-MUSIC spectrum and corresponding angles.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// - [`MusicError::RowCountMismatch`], [`MusicError::EmptyData`],
    ///   [`MusicError::NonFiniteData`] for unusable data, and
    ///   [`MusicError::DataShorterThanWindow`] if it has no complete STFT window.
    /// - [`MusicError::InvalidNfft`] if `nfft` is 0.
    /// - [`MusicError::TooManySources`] if `n_sources >= n_antennas`, [`MusicError::NoSources`]
    ///   if it is 0.
    /// - [`MusicError::NoUsableBins`] if none of the bins is in `1..=nfft / 2` (for `None`:
    ///   `nfft` is 1).
    /// - [`MusicError::SilentData`] if no usable bin has power.
    /// - [`MusicError::InvalidAngleGrid`], [`MusicError::InvalidSampleRate`] or
    ///   [`MusicError::InvalidAntennaPosition`] for an unusable estimator (see [`new`](Self::new)).
    pub fn ifb_music_spectrum(
        &self,
        data: &DMatrix<f64>,
        nfft: usize,
        n_sources: usize,
        bins: Option<&[usize]>,
    ) -> Result<(Vec<f64>, Vec<f64>)> {
        self.check_rows(data.nrows())?;
        self.check_sources(n_sources)?;
        self.check_array()?;
        let max_abs = check_real_samples(data)?;
        if nfft == 0 {
            return Err(MusicError::InvalidNfft);
        }
        if data.ncols() < nfft {
            return Err(MusicError::DataShorterThanWindow {
                nfft,
                samples: data.ncols(),
            });
        }
        let freq_bins = nfft / 2 + 1;

        let default_bins: Vec<usize> = (1..freq_bins).collect();
        let mut active_bins: Vec<usize> = bins
            .unwrap_or(&default_bins)
            .iter()
            .copied()
            .filter(|bin| (1..freq_bins).contains(bin))
            .collect();
        // A repeated bin would count more than once in the geometric mean; the order of the
        // bins does not change the mean.
        active_bins.sort_unstable();
        active_bins.dedup();
        if active_bins.is_empty() {
            return Err(MusicError::NoUsableBins);
        }

        // STFT per microphone channel (they share the cached FFT plan)
        let stfts: Vec<Vec<Vec<Cplx>>> = scaled_rows(data, max_abs)
            .iter()
            .map(|row| stft(row, nfft, 0))
            .collect::<Result<_>>()?;
        let n_windows = stfts[0][0].len();

        // Geometric mean, accumulated as a sum of logarithms: the product of hundreds of
        // per-bin spectra overflows f64.
        let mut log_sum: Option<Vec<f64>> = None;
        let mut angles_out: Vec<f64> = Vec::new();
        let mut n_processed = 0usize;

        // Silence is judged against the strongest bin of the whole spectrum, DC included,
        // so that a requested bin holding only rounding residue is still recognised.
        let strongest = stfts
            .iter()
            .fold(vec![0.0; freq_bins], |mut power, mic| {
                for (p, bin) in power.iter_mut().zip(mic) {
                    *p += bin.iter().map(|c| c.norm_sqr()).sum::<f64>() / n_windows as f64;
                }
                power
            })
            .into_iter()
            .fold(0.0, f64::max);

        for bin in active_bins {
            // Cross-spectral matrix of this bin, averaged over time windows. Built one bin
            // at a time so that only one n_mics x n_mics matrix is alive at once.
            let bin_slices: Vec<&[Cplx]> = stfts.iter().map(|s| s[bin].as_slice()).collect();
            let cov = cross_spectral_matrix(&bin_slices);
            if cov.trace().re <= SILENCE_RATIO * strongest {
                // No power in this bin: its noise subspace would be arbitrary.
                continue;
            }
            let frequency = bin as f64 * self.sample_rate / nfft as f64;
            let noise_mat = self.noise_subspace(&cov, n_sources)?;
            let (spec, angles) = self.spectrum(&noise_mat, frequency)?;

            match &mut log_sum {
                None => {
                    log_sum = Some(spec.iter().map(|s| s.ln()).collect());
                    angles_out = angles;
                }
                Some(sum) => {
                    for (acc, s) in sum.iter_mut().zip(spec.iter()) {
                        *acc += s.ln();
                    }
                }
            }
            n_processed += 1;
        }

        let sum = log_sum.ok_or(MusicError::SilentData)?;
        let merged: Vec<f64> = sum
            .iter()
            .map(|&v| (v / n_processed as f64).exp())
            .collect();
        Ok((merged, angles_out))
    }
}

<result>///
/// Functions that take data return [`MusicError`] for data they cannot use (wrong row
/// count, no samples, NaN, silence) and for invalid parameters (too many sources, an
/// unusable STFT size or bin list).
///
/// # Examples
/// ```
/// use musicrs::MusicEstimator;
/// let est = MusicEstimator::default(); // Kinect 4-mic array, 720 angle steps, [0, 2π)
/// ```
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct MusicEstimator {
    /// Antenna (microphone) positions as `[x, y]` pairs in metres.
    pub antenna_positions: Vec<[f64; 2]>,
    /// Number of angle steps in the angular search grid.
    pub angle_steps_num: usize,
    /// Angular search range `(start_rad, end_rad)`; the grid includes `start_rad` and
    /// excludes `end_rad`. A range spanning exactly 2π is treated as the full circle (its
    /// ends are adjacent when picking peaks); any other range is open at both ends.
    pub search_interval: (f64, f64),
    /// Sample rate of the input signal in Hz, used to determine the sign convention
    /// for the steering vector (positive exponent for f < sr/2, negative for f ≥ sr/2).
    pub sample_rate: f64,
}

impl Default for MusicEstimator {
    /// Returns an estimator configured for the 4-element Kinect microphone array
    /// with 720 angle steps over the full circle [0, 2π).
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            antenna_positions: DEFAULT_ANTENNA_POSITIONS.to_vec(),
            angle_steps_num: 720,
            search_interval: (0.0, 2.0 * PI),
            sample_rate: 16000.0,
        }
    }
}

impl MusicEstimator {
    /// Creates a new `MusicEstimator`.
    ///
    /// # Arguments
    /// * `antenna_positions` – Slice of `[x, y]` positions in metres.
    /// * `angle_steps_num`   – Number of discrete angles to evaluate.
    /// * `search_interval`   – `(start_rad, end_rad)` search range.
    /// * `sample_rate`       – Sample rate in Hz (used for aliasing-aware steering).
    ///
    /// Nothing is checked here, because the fields are public and can change later. The
    /// methods that use them return [`MusicError::InvalidAngleGrid`] unless
    /// `angle_steps_num > 0` and `search_interval` is finite with `start < end` and spans
    /// at most 2π, [`MusicError::InvalidSampleRate`] unless `sample_rate` is finite and
    /// positive, and [`MusicError::InvalidAntennaPosition`] for a NaN or infinite position.
    pub fn new(
        antenna_positions: Vec<[f64; 2]>,
        angle_steps_num: usize,
        search_interval: (f64, f64),
        sample_rate: f64,
    ) -> Self {
        Self {
            antenna_positions,
            angle_steps_num,
            search_interval,
            sample_rate,
        }
    }

    /// Number of antennas in the array.
    #[inline]
    pub fn n_antennas(&self) -> usize {
        self.antenna_positions.len()
    }

    /// Whether [`search_interval`](Self::search_interval) spans exactly the full circle,
    /// so that the first and last grid angles are neighbours.
    fn covers_full_circle(&self) -> bool {
        let (start, end) = self.search_interval;
        ((end - start).abs() - 2.0 * PI).abs() <= 1e-9
    }

    /// The search grid: `angle_steps_num` angles from `start` (included) to `end`
    /// (excluded). pyMUSIC asserts `start < end` in `MUSICEst.__init__`.
    fn angle_grid(&self) -> Result<Vec<f64>> {
        let (start, end) = self.search_interval;
        let steps = self.angle_steps_num;
        let usable = start.is_finite() && end.is_finite() && start < end;
        // A span of more than 2π (beyond the tolerance of `covers_full_circle`) would
        // visit some directions twice and report one source as two.
        if steps == 0 || !usable || end - start > 2.0 * PI + 1e-9 {
            return Err(MusicError::InvalidAngleGrid {
                angle_steps_num: steps,
                search_interval: self.search_interval,
            });
        }
        Ok((0..steps)
            .map(|i| start + (end - start) * i as f64 / steps as f64)
            .collect())
    }

    /// Checks the fields the steering vectors are built from: a finite, positive
    /// `sample_rate` and finite antenna positions.
    fn check_array(&self) -> Result<()> {
        if !(self.sample_rate.is_finite() && self.sample_rate > 0.0) {
            return Err(MusicError::InvalidSampleRate(self.sample_rate));
        }
        match self
            .antenna_positions
            .iter()
            .position(|p| !(p[0].is_finite() && p[1].is_finite()))
        {
            Some(index) => Err(MusicError::InvalidAntennaPosition { index }),
            None => Ok(()),
        }
    }

    fn check_rows(&self, got: usize) -> Result<()> {
        if got == self.n_antennas() {
            Ok(())
        } else {
            Err(MusicError::RowCountMismatch {
                expected: self.n_antennas(),
                got,
            })
        }
    }

    /// Checks that a signal frequency is finite and positive.
    fn check_frequency(frequency: f64) -> Result<()> {
        if frequency.is_finite() && frequency > 0.0 {
            Ok(())
        } else {
            Err(MusicError::InvalidFrequency(frequency))
        }
    }

    /// Checks that `0 < n_sources < n_antennas`. Zero sources would make the noise
    /// subspace the whole space and the spectrum meaningless.
    fn check_sources(&self, n_sources: usize) -> Result<()> {
        if n_sources >= self.n_antennas() {
            Err(MusicError::TooManySources {
                n_sources,
                n_antennas: self.n_antennas(),
            })
        } else if n_sources == 0 {
            Err(MusicError::NoSources)
        } else {
            Ok(())
        }
    }

    // ─── Core algorithm ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    /// Computes the steering vector for a plane wave arriving from `angle` (radians)
    /// at `frequency` (Hz).
    ///
    /// Element *j* is `exp(+i·2π·f·τⱼ)` where `τⱼ = (pⱼ · d̂) / c` is the projection of
    /// antenna *j*'s position onto the arrival direction, divided by the speed of sound. This
    /// matches the non-conjugated [`analytic_signal`] and STFT bins
    /// (pyMUSIC conjugates its analytic signal and uses `exp(−i·2π·f·τⱼ)`; the two agree below
    /// Nyquist). Relative to [`sample_rate`](Self::sample_rate):
    /// * above Nyquist the exponent is negated, `exp(−i·2π·f·τⱼ)`, because the recorded tone
    ///   is aliased and its phase is conjugated;
    /// * within 0.5 Hz of Nyquist the vector is real, `cos(2π·f·τⱼ)`, because the analytic
    ///   signal there is real too.
    ///
    /// # Examples
    /// ```
    /// use musicrs::MusicEstimator;
    /// let est = MusicEstimator::default();
    /// let sv = est.steering_vector(0.0, 300.0);
    /// assert_eq!(sv.len(), 4);
    /// // All elements have unit magnitude
    /// for c in sv.iter() {
    ///     assert!((c.norm() - 1.0).abs() < 1e-12);
    /// }
    /// ```
    pub fn steering_vector(&self, angle: f64, frequency: f64) -> CVec {
        let mut out = vec![Cplx::new(0.0, 0.0); self.n_antennas()];
        self.steering_vector_into(angle, frequency, &mut out);
        CVec::from_vec(out)
    }

    /// [`steering_vector`](Self::steering_vector) written into `out` (one element per
    /// antenna), so that the spectrum does not allocate a vector per angle.
    fn steering_vector_into(&self, angle: f64, frequency: f64, out: &mut [Cplx]) {
        let dir = [angle.cos(), angle.sin()];
        // For f < Nyquist (sr/2): analytic signal has positive phase → use +exponent.
        // For f > Nyquist: signal aliases in the one-sided FFT; dominant eigenvector
        // phase is conjugated → use −exponent.
        // At exactly Nyquist (f == sr/2): analytic signal is real; noise subspace is
        // also real → use cos(phase) as a real steering vector.
        let nyquist = self.sample_rate / 2.0;
        let phase_sign = if frequency > nyquist {
            -1.0_f64
        } else {
            1.0_f64
        };
        let at_nyquist = (frequency - nyquist).abs() < 0.5;
        for (element, p) in out.iter_mut().zip(&self.antenna_positions) {
            let delay = (p[0] * dir[0] + p[1] * dir[1]) / SPEED_OF_SOUND;
            let phase = phase_sign * 2.0 * PI * frequency * delay;
            *element = if at_nyquist {
                // Real steering vector: imaginary part is zero
                Cplx::new(phase.cos(), 0.0)
            } else {
                Cplx::from_polar(1.0, phase)
            };
        }
    }

    /// Extracts the noise subspace from the Hermitian covariance matrix `cov`.
    ///
    /// Eigendecomposes `cov`, sorts eigenvectors by ascending eigenvalue magnitude,
    /// and returns the `n − n_sources` columns spanning the noise subspace.
    ///
    /// # Arguments
    /// * `cov`       – Hermitian covariance matrix (n_antennas × n_antennas).
    /// * `n_sources` – Number of signal sources (must be in `1..n_antennas`).
    ///
    /// `cov` is assumed to be Hermitian, as every covariance matrix is: only its lower
    /// triangle (diagonal included) is read.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// [`MusicError::CovarianceShape`] if `cov` is not n_antennas × n_antennas,
    /// [`MusicError::NonFiniteData`] if it contains NaN or infinity,
    /// [`MusicError::TooManySources`] if `n_sources >= n_antennas`, and
    /// [`MusicError::NoSources`] if `n_sources` is 0.
    pub fn noise_subspace(&self, cov: &CMatrix, n_sources: usize) -> Result<CMatrix> {
        let n = self.n_antennas();
        if cov.shape() != (n, n) {
            return Err(MusicError::CovarianceShape {
                n_antennas: n,
                rows: cov.nrows(),
                cols: cov.ncols(),
            });
        }
        self.check_sources(n_sources)?;
        if !cov.iter().all(|c| c.re.is_finite() && c.im.is_finite()) {
            return Err(MusicError::NonFiniteData);
        }

        // Eigenvectors in ascending eigenvalue order; the first n_noise columns are the
        // noise subspace (smallest eigenvalues).
        let (_eigenvalues, eigenvectors) = hermitian_eigen(cov);
        let n_noise = cov.nrows() - n_sources;
        Ok(eigenvectors.columns(0, n_noise).into())
    }

    /// Generates the MUSIC pseudo-spectrum.
    ///
    /// For each angle θ in the search grid, the score is `1 / ‖Eₙᴴ · a(θ)‖²`.
    /// High values indicate signal directions of arrival.
    ///
    /// # Arguments
    /// * `noise_mat` – Noise subspace matrix (n_antennas × n_noise) from
    ///   [`noise_subspace`](Self::noise_subspace).
    /// * `frequency` – Signal frequency in Hz.
    ///
    /// # Returns
    /// `(spectrum, angles)` — corresponding vectors of the same length.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// - [`MusicError::RowCountMismatch`] if `noise_mat` does not have one row per antenna.
    /// - [`MusicError::InvalidFrequency`] unless `frequency` is finite and positive.
    /// - [`MusicError::InvalidAngleGrid`], [`MusicError::InvalidSampleRate`] or
    ///   [`MusicError::InvalidAntennaPosition`] for an unusable estimator (see [`new`](Self::new)).
    pub fn spectrum(&self, noise_mat: &CMatrix, frequency: f64) -> Result<(Vec<f64>, Vec<f64>)> {
        self.check_rows(noise_mat.nrows())?;
        self.check_array()?;
        Self::check_frequency(frequency)?;
        let angles = self.angle_grid()?;
        let mut a = vec![Cplx::new(0.0, 0.0); self.n_antennas()];
        let scores: Vec<f64> = angles
            .iter()
            .map(|&theta| {
                self.steering_vector_into(theta, frequency, &mut a);
                // ‖Eₙᴴ a‖²: one inner product per noise eigenvector (column of noise_mat)
                let denom: f64 = noise_mat
                    .column_iter()
                    .map(|e| {
                        e.iter()
                            .zip(&a)
                            .map(|(e, a)| e.conj() * a)
                            .sum::<Cplx>()
                            .norm_sqr()
                    })
                    .sum();
                if denom == 0.0 {
                    f64::INFINITY
                } else {
                    1.0 / denom
                }
            })
            .collect();

        Ok((scores, angles))
    }

    /// Estimates the directions of arrival for `n_sources` narrowband sources.
    ///
    /// # Arguments
    /// * `data`      – Complex array data (n_antennas × n_samples).
    /// * `n_sources` – Number of sources to detect.
    /// * `frequency` – Signal frequency in Hz.
    ///
    /// # Returns
    /// Up to `n_sources` estimated angles (radians), sorted by descending peak height.
    ///
    /// The sources must be uncorrelated. Coherent sources (the same tone from two
    /// directions with a fixed phase relation, such as two loudspeakers on one signal or a
    /// reflection) give a covariance of rank 1, like a single source, and the estimates
    /// point in neither direction.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// - [`MusicError::RowCountMismatch`] if `data` does not have one row per antenna.
    /// - [`MusicError::EmptyData`] if it has no samples, [`MusicError::NonFiniteData`]
    ///   if it contains NaN or infinity, [`MusicError::SilentData`] if it is all zeros.
    /// - [`MusicError::TooManySources`] if `n_sources >= n_antennas`, [`MusicError::NoSources`]
    ///   if it is 0.
    /// - [`MusicError::InvalidFrequency`] unless `frequency` is finite and positive.
    /// - [`MusicError::InvalidAngleGrid`], [`MusicError::InvalidSampleRate`] or
    ///   [`MusicError::InvalidAntennaPosition`] for an unusable estimator (see [`new`](Self::new)).
    pub fn estimate_doa(
        &self,
        data: &CMatrix,
        n_sources: usize,
        frequency: f64,
    ) -> Result<Vec<f64>> {
        self.check_rows(data.nrows())?;
        self.check_sources(n_sources)?;
        self.check_array()?;
        Self::check_frequency(frequency)?;
        if data.ncols() == 0 {
            return Err(MusicError::EmptyData);
        }
        if !data.iter().all(|c| c.re.is_finite() && c.im.is_finite()) {
            return Err(MusicError::NonFiniteData);
        }
        let max_abs = data
            .iter()
            .fold(0.0, |m: f64, c| m.max(c.re.abs()).max(c.im.abs()));
        let scale = power_of_two_scale(max_abs);
        let data = data.map(|c| c / scale);
        let n_samples = data.ncols() as f64;
        let cov = (&data * data.adjoint()).scale(1.0 / n_samples);
        self.doa_from_covariance(&cov, n_sources, frequency)
    }

    /// The DOA estimates of `estimate_doa` from the covariance `cov` of the array data.
    fn doa_from_covariance(
        &self,
        cov: &CMatrix,
        n_sources: usize,
        frequency: f64,
    ) -> Result<Vec<f64>> {
        if cov.trace().re == 0.0 {
            return Err(MusicError::SilentData);
        }
        let noise_mat = self.noise_subspace(cov, n_sources)?;
        let (scores, angles) = self.spectrum(&noise_mat, frequency)?;
        Ok(find_peaks(
            &scores,
            &angles,
            n_sources,
            self.covers_full_circle(),
        ))
    }

    /// Estimates DOAs from real-valued microphone data, like pyMUSIC's `getSourceAngles`.
    ///
    /// Removes each channel's mean and estimates the DOAs from the covariance of the
    /// channels' analytic signals (as [`analytic_signal`] gives them), with the same
    /// eigendecomposition, spectrum and peak search as [`estimate_doa`](Self::estimate_doa).
    /// Without the mean removal a DC offset acts as a second source at broadside.
    ///
    /// The analytic signals are never formed, and `estimate_doa` is not called: the
    /// covariance is computed directly from the real FFT of each channel (by Parseval's
    /// theorem), which gives the same covariance up to rounding at a fraction of the cost.
    /// The data is scaled by a power of two before that, which is exact, so the covariance
    /// is not rescaled again as `estimate_doa` does with complex data.
    ///
    /// # Arguments
    /// * `data`      – Real array data (n_antennas × n_samples).
    /// * `n_sources` – Number of sources to detect.
    /// * `frequency` – Signal frequency in Hz.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// As [`estimate_doa`](Self::estimate_doa); data that is constant on every channel (its
    /// energy after removing the mean is 260 dB below the input's) is
    /// [`MusicError::SilentData`].
    ///
    /// # Examples
    /// ```
    /// use musicrs::MusicEstimator;
    /// use nalgebra::DMatrix;
    /// use std::f64::consts::PI;
    ///
    /// let est = MusicEstimator::default();
    /// let (freq, doa, sr) = (1000.0, 60.0_f64.to_radians(), est.sample_rate);
    /// // Plane wave: microphone j hears the source delayed by -(p_j · d) / c
    /// let data = DMatrix::from_fn(4, 4000, |j, t| {
    ///     let p = est.antenna_positions[j];
    ///     let advance = (p[0] * doa.cos() + p[1] * doa.sin()) / 343.2;
    ///     (2.0 * PI * freq * (t as f64 / sr + advance)).cos()
    /// });
    /// let angles = est.estimate_doa_from_real(&data, 1, freq)?;
    /// // A linear array cannot tell θ from 360° − θ
    /// let deg = angles[0].to_degrees();
    /// assert!((deg - 60.0).abs() < 2.0 || (deg - 300.0).abs() < 2.0, "got {deg}");
    /// # Ok::<(), musicrs::MusicError>(())
    /// ```
    pub fn estimate_doa_from_real(
        &self,
        data: &DMatrix<f64>,
        n_sources: usize,
        frequency: f64,
    ) -> Result<Vec<f64>> {
        self.check_rows(data.nrows())?;
        self.check_sources(n_sources)?;
        self.check_array()?;
        Self::check_frequency(frequency)?;
        let max_abs = check_real_samples(data)?;
        let mut rows = scaled_rows(data, max_abs);
        let (mut raw_energy, mut centred_energy) = (0.0, 0.0);
        for row in &mut rows {
            let mean = accurate_mean(row.iter());
            for x in row.iter_mut() {
                raw_energy += *x * *x;
                *x -= mean;
                centred_energy += *x * *x;
            }
        }
        if centred_energy <= SILENCE_RATIO * raw_energy {
            return Err(MusicError::SilentData);
        }
        let cov = analytic_covariance(&mut rows);
        self.doa_from_covariance(&cov, n_sources, frequency)
    }

    /// Integrated Frequency-Band (IFB) MUSIC spectrum.
    ///
    /// Computes a narrowband MUSIC spectrum at each frequency bin and combines them
    /// via geometric mean for improved wideband robustness.
    ///
    /// # Arguments
    /// * `data`          – Real-valued microphone data (n_antennas × n_samples).
    /// * `nfft`          – STFT window size.
    /// * `n_sources`     – Number of sources.
    /// * `bins`          – Frequency bin indices to use; `None` uses all bins except DC.
    ///   The DC bin 0 (it has no direction information), bins at or above `nfft / 2 + 1`
    ///   and bins with no power are ignored. Each bin counts once in the geometric mean,
    ///   however often it is listed and in whatever order.
    ///
    /// Bin frequencies are derived from [`MusicEstimator::sample_rate`], the same rate
    /// [`steering_vector`](Self::steering_vector) uses for its Nyquist handling.
    /// Bins only cover `[0, sample_rate / 2]`, so a tone recorded above Nyquist is
    /// steered at its aliased frequency and its DOA cannot be recovered here.
    ///
    /// # Returns
    /// `(spectrum, angles)` — the IFB-MUSIC spectrum and corresponding angles.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// - [`MusicError::RowCountMismatch`], [`MusicError::EmptyData`],
    ///   [`MusicError::NonFiniteData`] for unusable data, and
    ///   [`MusicError::DataShorterThanWindow`] if it has no complete STFT window.
    /// - [`MusicError::InvalidNfft`] if `nfft` is 0.
    /// - [`MusicError::TooManySources`] if `n_sources >= n_antennas`, [`MusicError::NoSources`]
    ///   if it is 0.
    /// - [`MusicError::NoUsableBins`] if none of the bins is in `1..=nfft / 2` (for `None`:
    ///   `nfft` is 1).
    /// - [`MusicError::SilentData`] if no usable bin has power.
    /// - [`MusicError::InvalidAngleGrid`], [`MusicError::InvalidSampleRate`] or
    ///   [`MusicError::InvalidAntennaPosition`] for an unusable estimator (see [`new`](Self::new)).
    pub fn ifb_music_spectrum(
        &self,
        data: &DMatrix<f64>,
        nfft: usize,
        n_sources: usize,
        bins: Option<&[usize]>,
    ) -> Result<(Vec<f64>, Vec<f64>)> {
        self.check_rows(data.nrows())?;
        self.check_sources(n_sources)?;
        self.check_array()?;
        let max_abs = check_real_samples(data)?;
        if nfft == 0 {
            return Err(MusicError::InvalidNfft);
        }
        if data.ncols() < nfft {
            return Err(MusicError::DataShorterThanWindow {
                nfft,
                samples: data.ncols(),
            });
        }
        let freq_bins = nfft / 2 + 1;

        let default_bins: Vec<usize> = (1..freq_bins).collect();
        let mut active_bins: Vec<usize> = bins
            .unwrap_or(&default_bins)
            .iter()
            .copied()
            .filter(|bin| (1..freq_bins).contains(bin))
            .collect();
        // A repeated bin would count more than once in the geometric mean; the order of the
        // bins does not change the mean.
        active_bins.sort_unstable();
        active_bins.dedup();
        if active_bins.is_empty() {
            return Err(MusicError::NoUsableBins);
        }

        // STFT per microphone channel (they share the cached FFT plan)
        let stfts: Vec<Vec<Vec<Cplx>>> = scaled_rows(data, max_abs)
            .iter()
            .map(|row| stft(row, nfft, 0))
            .collect::<Result<_>>()?;
        let n_windows = stfts[0][0].len();

        // Geometric mean, accumulated as a sum of logarithms: the product of hundreds of
        // per-bin spectra overflows f64.
        let mut log_sum: Option<Vec<f64>> = None;
        let mut angles_out: Vec<f64> = Vec::new();
        let mut n_processed = 0usize;

        // Silence is judged against the strongest bin of the whole spectrum, DC included,
        // so that a requested bin holding only rounding residue is still recognised.
        let strongest = stfts
            .iter()
            .fold(vec![0.0; freq_bins], |mut power, mic| {
                for (p, bin) in power.iter_mut().zip(mic) {
                    *p += bin.iter().map(|c| c.norm_sqr()).sum::<f64>() / n_windows as f64;
                }
                power
            })
            .into_iter()
            .fold(0.0, f64::max);

        for bin in active_bins {
            // Cross-spectral matrix of this bin, averaged over time windows. Built one bin
            // at a time so that only one n_mics x n_mics matrix is alive at once.
            let bin_slices: Vec<&[Cplx]> = stfts.iter().map(|s| s[bin].as_slice()).collect();
            let cov = cross_spectral_matrix(&bin_slices);
            if cov.trace().re <= SILENCE_RATIO * strongest {
                // No power in this bin: its noise subspace would be arbitrary.
                continue;
            }
            let frequency = bin as f64 * self.sample_rate / nfft as f64;
            let noise_mat = self.noise_subspace(&cov, n_sources)?;
            let (spec, angles) = self.spectrum(&noise_mat, frequency)?;

            match &mut log_sum {
                None => {
                    log_sum = Some(spec.iter().map(|s| s.ln()).collect());
                    angles_out = angles;
                }
                Some(sum) => {
                    for (acc, s) in sum.iter_mut().zip(spec.iter()) {
                        *acc += s.ln();
                    }
                }
            }
            n_processed += 1;
        }

        let sum = log_sum.ok_or(MusicError::SilentData)?;
        let merged: Vec<f64> = sum
            .iter()
            .map(|&v| (v / n_processed as f64).exp())
            .collect();
        Ok((merged, angles_out))
    }
}

I read `src/music.rs`, `src/error.rs`, `src/lib.rs` and the README. Here is a plan; some API and convention decisions need your answer before I write code.

# Plan: 3-D DOA estimation (azimuth + elevation)

## What changes conceptually

Today everything is planar. Positions are `[x, y]`, the steering vector uses `d̂ = (cos θ, sin θ)`, the grid is a 1-D list of angles, and `find_peaks` works on a 1-D, optionally circular, list. For 3-D:

- **Positions** become `[x, y, z]`.
- **Direction** becomes `d̂ = (cos el·cos az, cos el·sin az, sin el)`, and the delay is still `τⱼ = pⱼ·d̂ / c`. The sign convention and the Nyquist handling (sign flip above Nyquist, real vector at Nyquist) stay as they are.
- **Grid** becomes 2-D: azimuth × elevation.
- **Peak picking** becomes 2-D. Azimuth wraps around when the grid covers the full circle; elevation is open at both ends.
- **Covariance, eigendecomposition and noise subspace don't change.** `analytic_covariance`, `cross_spectral_matrix`, `noise_subspace` and the STFT don't depend on geometry, so the real-data and IFB preprocessing can be reused as they are.

## Proposed API (recommended, to be confirmed)

Add a separate `MusicEstimator3d` and leave `MusicEstimator` as it is. Changing `MusicEstimator` would break every caller because of the `[f64; 2]` field.

```rust
pub struct MusicEstimator3d {
    pub antenna_positions: Vec<[f64; 3]>,
    pub azimuth_steps: usize,
    pub azimuth_interval: (f64, f64),     // like search_interval; a 2π span wraps
    pub elevation_steps: usize,
    pub elevation_interval: (f64, f64),   // within [-π/2, π/2]
    pub sample_rate: f64,
}
pub struct Direction { pub azimuth: f64, pub elevation: f64 }

impl MusicEstimator3d {
    pub fn steering_vector(&self, dir: Direction, frequency: f64) -> CVec;
    pub fn noise_subspace(&self, cov, n_sources) -> Result<CMatrix>;
    pub fn spectrum(&self, noise, frequency) -> Result<Spectrum3d>; // elevation × azimuth DMatrix plus both grids
    pub fn estimate_doa(&self, data: &CMatrix, n, f) -> Result<Vec<Direction>>;
    pub fn estimate_doa_from_real(&self, data: &DMatrix<f64>, n, f) -> Result<Vec<Direction>>;
    pub fn ifb_music_spectrum(&self, data, nfft, n, bins) -> Result<Spectrum3d>;
}
```

To avoid duplicating code, both estimators would share private helpers. The steering vector would be built from a precomputed unit direction (or a delay vector), and the spectrum loop would run over a slice of directions. Both front ends become thin wrappers over that.

## Steps (one commit each, each builds and passes tests)

1. **Refactor, no change in behaviour.** Move the steering vector, spectrum loop, Nyquist handling, the real-data/IFB preprocessing and the validation helpers into geometry-independent private functions. `MusicEstimator` keeps its current output: the golden tests, snapshots and DOA tests must not change.
2. **Add the 3-D types and steering vector.** This covers `Direction`, `MusicEstimator3d`, the az/el grid, `check_array` for 3-D positions, and unit tests for the phase, unit magnitude and Nyquist cases.
3. **Add a 2-D peak finder.** A peak is a run of equal values, connected over the 8 neighbours, that is higher than every point around it, reported at its centre. Azimuth wraps when the grid covers the full circle. Unit tests mirror the existing `find_peaks_*` ones: wrap-around, plateaus, edges and a constant spectrum.
4. **Narrowband 3-D estimation.** This adds `spectrum`, `estimate_doa` and `estimate_doa_from_real`, reusing `analytic_covariance`.
5. **IFB-MUSIC in 3-D.** The geometric mean over bins works on the 2-D grid.
6. **Errors.** Add `InvalidElevationGrid`, reuse `InvalidAngleGrid` for azimuth, and extend `errors_test.rs`.
7. **Tests** in `tests/synthetic_3d_test.rs` (synthetic plane waves):
   - A tetrahedral or cube array estimates 1–3 sources at various elevations, including near the zenith, within one grid step.
   - **Link to the 2-D code:** with z = 0 and the elevation grid fixed at {0}, the 3-D spectrum must equal the 2-D spectrum exactly, on the Kinect WAVs too. This ties the new path to the pyMUSIC-validated one.
   - A planar array finds the correct |elevation| on a hemisphere grid, and the test documents the up/down mirror.
   - Noisy data, the real-data path, and IFB on multi-tone signals.
   - Mark slow cases `#[ignore = "slow"]`.
8. **Docs.** Update the README (usage and the "things to keep in mind" list for array ambiguities), `lib.rs`, the CLAUDE.md architecture and test list, and maybe a 3-D benchmark row.

## Risks and limits to document

- **Array geometry decides what can be resolved.** A linear array (like the Kinect) only gives the cone angle around its axis. A planar array cannot tell +el from −el. Only a non-planar array resolves the whole sphere. I'd document this rather than return an error.
- **Poles.** At ±90° every azimuth points in the same direction, so one source shows up as a whole row of peaks. I'd use elevation grids that leave out the poles by default, or merge the pole row into one point.
- **Cost.** A 720 × 360 grid has about 260k directions, roughly 360× the work of the 2-D spectrum (tens of ms). Precomputing the direction vectors helps. A coarse-to-fine search is possible later but is out of scope here.
- **Test data.** There is no real 3-D recording and no pyMUSIC reference, so 3-D correctness rests on the synthetic tests plus the exact match with the 2-D spectrum.

## Questions for you

1. **API shape:** a separate `MusicEstimator3d` (my recommendation), or generalise `MusicEstimator` to 3-D positions (a breaking change)?
2. **Elevation convention:** elevation from the horizontal plane (−90° to +90°, my recommendation), or the polar angle from +z (0° to 180°)?
3. **Grid:** a regular az × el grid (simple, and peak picking stays easy to reason about), or a uniform grid on the sphere (e.g. a Fibonacci grid: no crowding at the poles, but peak picking needs a neighbour graph)?
4. **Scope:** narrowband and IFB in this change, or narrowband first and IFB in a follow-up PR?
5. **Do you have real recordings with known elevation, or a specific 3-D array** (e.g. ReSpeaker or a tetrahedral mic) that the tests should model?
6. **Breaking changes:** `MusicError` isn't `#[non_exhaustive]`, so adding a variant is technically breaking. Is a minor-version bump fine, and should I mark it `#[non_exhaustive]` while we're at it?
7. **Branch:** the worktree is on `amjadsaadeh/3d-estimation`, but CLAUDE.md asks for `feat/<name>`. Should I create `feat/3d-doa`, or keep the current branch?

    '2:name = "musicrs"\n' +

  '// DOA estimation on synthetic plane waves with arrays other than the Kinect line.\n' +

    '\n' +
    'mod common;\n' +
    '\n' +
    'use std::f64::consts::PI;\n' +
    '\n' +
    'use musicrs::{MusicError, MusicEstimator, select_bins_by_energy};\n' +
    'use nalgebra::DMatrix;\n' +
    'use num_complex::Complex;\n' +
    '\n' +
    'const SPEED_OF_SOUND: f64 = 343.2;\n' +
    'const SAMPLE_RATE: f64 = 16000.0;\n' +
    '\n' +
    '/// Square array, 10 cm side, centred on the origin.\n' +
    'fn square_array() -> MusicEstimator {\n' +
    '    MusicEstimator::new(\n' +
    '        vec![[0.05, 0.05], [-0.05, 0.05], [-0.05, -0.05], [0.05, -0.05]],\n' +
    '        720,\n' +
    '        (0.0, 2.0 * PI),\n' +

    '\n' +
    '/// Time by which a plane wave from `doa` reaches `p` ahead of the origin.\n' +
    'fn advance(p: [f64; 2], doa: f64) -> f64 {\n' +

    '\n' +
    '/// Deterministic pseudo-random values in [0, 1) (LCG).\n' +
    'fn uniform(n: usize, seed: u64) -> Vec<f64> {\n' +
    '    let mut state = seed;\n' +
    '    (0..n)\n' +
    '        .map(|_| {\n' +
    '            state = state\n' +
    '                .wrapping_mul(6_364_136_223_846_793_005)\n' +
    '                .wrapping_add(1_442_695_040_888_963_407);\n' +
    '            (state >> 11) as f64 / (1u64 << 53) as f64\n' +
    '        })\n' +
    '        .collect()\n' +
    '}\n' +
    '\n' +
    'fn assert_angles(found: &[f64], truths_deg: &[f64], tolerance_deg: f64) {\n' +

    '    for &truth in truths_deg {\n' +
    '        let error = found_deg\n' +
    '            .iter()\n' +
    '            .map(|&f| common::angular_error(f, &[truth]))\n' +
    '            .fold(f64::INFINITY, f64::min);\n' +
    '        assert!(\n' +
    '            error <= tolerance_deg,\n' +
    '            "expected {truth}° among {found_deg:?} (error {error:.2}°)"\n' +
    '        );\n' +
    '    }\n' +
    '}\n' +
    '\n' +
    '/// A real-valued tone through `estimate_doa_from_real` is located at its true angle\n' +
    '/// all around the circle, with no mirror image.\n' +
    '#[test]\n' +
    'fn square_array_single_real_source() {\n' +
    '    let est = square_array();\n' +
    '    let freq = 1000.0;\n' +
    '    for doa_deg in [0.0, 50.0, 135.0, 200.0, 300.0] {\n' +
    '        let doa = f64::to_radians(doa_deg);\n' +
    '        let data = DMatrix::from_fn(4, 4000, |m, t| {\n' +
    '            let p = est.antenna_positions[m];\n' +
    '            (2.0 * PI * freq * (t as f64 / SAMPLE_RATE + advance(p, doa))).cos()\n' +
    '        });\n' +
    '        assert_angles(\n' +
    '            &est.estimate_doa_from_real(&data, 1, freq).unwrap(),\n' +
    '            &[doa_deg],\n' +
    '            1.0,\n' +
    '        );\n' +
    '    }\n' +
    '}\n' +
    '\n' +
    '/// Two uncorrelated sources at the same frequency, plus a little noise, are both found.\n' +
    '#[test]\n' +
    'fn square_array_two_sources() {\n' +
    '    let est = square_array();\n' +
    '    let freq = 1500.0;\n' +
    '    let n_samples = 4000;\n' +
    '    let doas_deg = [50.0_f64, 200.0];\n' +
    '    let jitter = uniform(n_samples, 3);\n' +

    '    let data = DMatrix::from_fn(4, n_samples, |m, t| {\n' +
    '        let p = est.antenna_positions[m];\n' +
    '        let t_s = t as f64 / SAMPLE_RATE;\n' +
    '        // Source 2 gets a random phase per sample, which decorrelates it from source 1\n' +
    '        let phases = [0.0, 2.0 * PI * jitter[t]];\n' +
    '        let sources: Complex<f64> = doas_deg\n' +
    '            .iter()\n' +
    '            .zip(phases)\n' +
    '            .map(|(&d, phi)| {\n' +
    '                Complex::from_polar(\n' +
    '                    1.0,\n' +
    '                    2.0 * PI * freq * (t_s + advance(p, d.to_radians())) + phi,\n' +
    '                )\n' +
    '            })\n' +
    '            .sum();\n' +
    '        let i = 2 * (m * n_samples + t);\n' +
    '        sources + Complex::new(noise[i] - 0.5, noise[i + 1] - 0.5).scale(0.05)\n' +
    '    });\n' +
    '    assert_angles(&est.estimate_doa(&data, 2, freq).unwrap(), &doas_deg, 1.0);\n' +

    '#[test]\n' +
    'fn coherent_sources_are_not_resolved() {\n' +
    '    let est = square_array();\n' +
    '    let freq = 1500.0;\n' +
    '    let n_samples = 4000;\n' +
    '    let doas_deg = [50.0_f64, 200.0];\n' +
    '    let jitter = uniform(n_samples, 3);\n' +
    '    let waves = |decorrelate: bool| {\n' +
    '        DMatrix::from_fn(4, n_samples, |m, t| {\n' +
    '            let p = est.antenna_positions[m];\n' +
    '            let t_s = t as f64 / SAMPLE_RATE;\n' +

    '                    1.0\n' +
    '                },\n' +
    '            ];\n' +
    '            doas_deg\n' +
    '                .iter()\n' +
    '                .zip(phases)\n' +
    '                .map(|(&d, phi)| {\n' +
    '                    Complex::from_polar(\n' +
    '                        1.0,\n' +
    '                        2.0 * PI * freq * (t_s + advance(p, d.to_radians())) + phi,\n' +
    '                    )\n' +
    '                })\n' +
    '                .sum::<Complex<f64>>()\n' +
    '        })\n' +
    '    };\n' +
    '    assert_angles(\n' +
    '        &est.estimate_doa(&waves(true), 2, freq).unwrap(),\n' +
    '        &doas_deg,\n' +
    '        1.0,\n' +

    '    let coherent = est.estimate_doa(&waves(false), 2, freq).unwrap();\n' +

    '\n' +
    '/// Three sources on a five-element array (the most an n-element array resolves is n − 1).\n' +
    '#[test]\n' +
    'fn pentagon_array_three_sources() {\n' +
    '    let positions: Vec<[f64; 2]> = (0..5)\n' +
    '        .map(|k| {\n' +
    '            let a = 2.0 * PI * k as f64 / 5.0;\n' +
    '            [0.06 * a.cos(), 0.06 * a.sin()]\n' +
    '        })\n' +
    '        .collect();\n' +
    '    let est = MusicEstimator::new(positions, 720, (0.0, 2.0 * PI), SAMPLE_RATE);\n' +
    '    let freq = 1200.0;\n' +
    '    let n_samples = 6000;\n' +
    '    let doas_deg = [30.0_f64, 150.0, 260.0];\n' +
    '    let jitter = uniform(2 * n_samples, 9);\n' +
    '    let noise = uniform(10 * n_samples, 13);\n' +
    '    let data = DMatrix::from_fn(5, n_samples, |m, t| {\n' +
    '        let p = est.antenna_positions[m];\n' +
    '        let t_s = t as f64 / SAMPLE_RATE;\n' +
    '        let phases = [0.0, 2.0 * PI * jitter[t], 2.0 * PI * jitter[n_samples + t]];\n' +
    '        let sources: Complex<f64> = doas_deg\n' +
    '            .iter()\n' +
    '            .zip(phases)\n' +
    '            .map(|(&d, phi)| {\n' +
    '                Complex::from_polar(\n' +
    '                    1.0,\n' +
    '                    2.0 * PI * freq * (t_s + advance(p, d.to_radians())) + phi,\n' +
    '                )\n' +
    '            })\n' +
    '            .sum();\n' +
    '        let i = 2 * (m * n_samples + t);\n' +
    '        sources + Complex::new(noise[i] - 0.5, noise[i + 1] - 0.5).scale(0.05)\n' +
    '    });\n' +
    '    assert_angles(&est.estimate_doa(&data, 3, freq).unwrap(), &doas_deg, 1.0);\n' +
    '}\n' +
    '\n' +
    "/// The Kinect line array's spectrum is mirror-symmetric (θ ≡ 360° − θ). A source at\n" +
    '/// endfire that falls between two grid points therefore scores exactly the same on both,\n' +
    '/// and must still be found, at the midpoint between them.\n' +
    '#[test]\n' +
    'fn line_array_endfire_between_grid_points() {\n' +
    '    let half_step = 0.25_f64.to_radians();\n' +
    '    let cases = [\n' +
    '        // 719 steps: 180° lies midway between two grid points\n' +
    '        (\n' +
    '            MusicEstimator {\n' +
    '                angle_steps_num: 719,\n' +
    '                ..MusicEstimator::default()\n' +
    '            },\n' +
    '            180.0,\n' +
    '        ),\n' +
    '        // Grid shifted by half a step: 0° lies midway between -0.25° and 0.25°\n' +
    '        (\n' +
    '            MusicEstimator {\n' +
    '                search_interval: (-half_step, 2.0 * PI - half_step),\n' +
    '                ..MusicEstimator::default()\n' +
    '            },\n' +
    '            0.0,\n' +
    '        ),\n' +
    '    ];\n' +
    '    let freq = 1000.0;\n' +
    '    for (est, doa_deg) in cases {\n' +
    '        let doa = f64::to_radians(doa_deg);\n' +
    '        let data = DMatrix::from_fn(4, 4000, |m, t| {\n' +
    '            let p = est.antenna_positions[m];\n' +
    '            (2.0 * PI * freq * (t as f64 / SAMPLE_RATE + advance(p, doa))).cos()\n' +
    '        });\n' +
    '        assert_angles(\n' +
    '            &est.estimate_doa_from_real(&data, 1, freq).unwrap(),\n' +
    '            &[doa_deg],\n' +
    '            0.01,\n' +
    '        );\n' +
    '    }\n' +
    '}\n' +
    '\n' +
    "/// A Kinect-array plane wave at `freq` from `doa_deg`, sampled at the estimator's rate.\n" +
    'fn kinect_tone(est: &MusicEstimator, freq: f64, doa_deg: f64, n_samples: usize) -> DMatrix<f64> {\n' +
    '    let doa = f64::to_radians(doa_deg);\n' +
    '    DMatrix::from_fn(4, n_samples, |m, t| {\n' +
    '        let p = est.antenna_positions[m];\n' +
    '        (2.0 * PI * freq * (t as f64 / est.sample_rate + advance(p, doa))).cos()\n' +
    '    })\n' +
    '}\n' +
    '\n' +
    '/// Very loud and very quiet recordings give the same answer: the data is rescaled before\n' +
    '/// its energy and covariance are computed, which would otherwise overflow (or underflow).\n' +
    '#[test]\n' +
    'fn extreme_amplitudes() {\n' +
    '    let est = MusicEstimator {\n' +
    '        search_interval: (0.0, PI),\n' +
    '        angle_steps_num: 360,\n' +
    '        ..MusicEstimator::default()\n' +
    '    };\n' +
    '    let data = kinect_tone(&est, 1000.0, 40.0, 4000);\n' +
    '    let argmax = |s: &[f64]| (0..s.len()).max_by(|&a, &b| s[a].total_cmp(&s[b])).unwrap();\n' +

    '        let scaled = &data * amplitude;\n' +
    '        let found = est.estimate_doa_from_real(&scaled, 1, 1000.0).unwrap();\n' +
    '        assert_eq!(found.len(), 1, "amplitude {amplitude}");\n' +
    '        assert!(\n' +
    '            (found[0].to_degrees() - 40.0).abs() <= 0.5,\n' +
    '            "amplitude {amplitude}: got {found:?}"\n' +
    '        );\n' +
    '        let (spectrum, angles) = est\n' +
    '            .ifb_music_spectrum(&scaled, 160, 1, Some(&[10]))\n' +
    '            .unwrap();\n' +

    '        assert!(\n' +
    '            (peak - 40.0).abs() <= 0.5,\n' +
    '            "amplitude {amplitude}: IFB peak {peak}°"\n' +
    '        );\n' +
    '    }\n' +
    '}\n' +
    '\n' +
    '/// A quiet tone on a large DC offset is still found, narrowband and with IFB, whose\n' +
    '/// silence check compares each bin with the strongest bin, DC included.\n' +
    '#[test]\n' +
    'fn quiet_tone_on_large_offset() {\n' +
    '    let est = MusicEstimator {\n' +
    '        search_interval: (0.0, PI),\n' +
    '        angle_steps_num: 360,\n' +
    '        ..MusicEstimator::default()\n' +
    '    };\n' +
    '    let data = kinect_tone(&est, 1000.0, 40.0, 4000).map(|x| 1e6 + 1e-5 * x);\n' +
    '    let found = est.estimate_doa_from_real(&data, 1, 1000.0).unwrap();\n' +
    '    assert!((found[0].to_degrees() - 40.0).abs() <= 0.5, "got {found:?}");\n' +
    '    let (spectrum, angles) = est.ifb_music_spectrum(&data, 160, 1, Some(&[10])).unwrap();\n' +
    '    let peak = (0..spectrum.len())\n' +
    '        .max_by(|&a, &b| spectrum[a].total_cmp(&spectrum[b]))\n' +
    '        .unwrap();\n' +
    '    assert!(\n' +
    '        (angles[peak].to_degrees() - 40.0).abs() <= 0.5,\n' +
    '        "IFB peak {}°",\n' +
    '        angles[peak].to_degrees()\n' +
    '    );\n' +
    '}\n' +
    '\n' +
    '/// A one-point grid on an open interval reports its only angle.\n' +
    '#[test]\n' +

    '        angle_steps_num: 1,\n' +
    '        search_interval: (0.0, PI),\n' +
    '        ..MusicEstimator::default()\n' +
    '    };\n' +
    '    let data = kinect_tone(&est, 1000.0, 40.0, 1000);\n' +
    '    assert_eq!(est.estimate_doa_from_real(&data, 1, 1000.0), Ok(vec![0.0]));\n' +

    '\n' +

    '#[test]\n' +

    '    let data = kinect_tone(&est, 1000.0, 40.0, 1000);\n' +
    '    let no_grid = MusicEstimator {\n' +
    '        angle_steps_num: 0,\n' +
    '        ..MusicEstimator::default()\n' +

    '    assert!(matches!(\n' +
    '        no_grid.estimate_doa_from_real(&data, 1, 1000.0),\n' +

    '        est.estimate_doa_from_real(&data, 0, 1000.0),\n' +
    '        Err(MusicError::NoSources)\n' +
    '    );\n' +
    '    assert_eq!(\n' +
    '        est.estimate_doa_from_real(&data, 1, 0.0),\n' +
    '        Err(MusicError::InvalidFrequency(0.0))\n' +
    '    );\n' +
    '}\n' +
    '\n' +
    '/// Very short recordings: two or three samples still give an estimate. A single sample\n' +

    '    let est = MusicEstimator::default();\n' +

    '        assert!(doa(n).is_ok(), "n = {n}: {:?}", doa(n));\n' +
    '    }\n' +
    '}\n' +
    '\n' +
    '/// IFB-MUSIC and bin selection at 48 kHz: bin frequencies follow `sample_rate`.\n' +
    '/// nfft = 480 gives 100 Hz bins, so the 1 kHz tone is bin 10.\n' +
    '#[test]\n' +
    'fn ifb_at_48_khz() {\n' +
    '    let est = MusicEstimator {\n' +
    '        sample_rate: 48000.0,\n' +
    '        ..MusicEstimator::default()\n' +
    '    };\n' +
    '    let data = kinect_tone(&est, 1000.0, 40.0, 48000);\n' +
    '    let bins = select_bins_by_energy(&data, 480, 20.0).unwrap();\n' +
    '    assert_eq!(bins, [10]);\n' +
    '    let (spectrum, angles) = est.ifb_music_spectrum(&data, 480, 1, Some(&bins)).unwrap();\n' +
    '    let argmax = (0..spectrum.len())\n' +
    '        .max_by(|&a, &b| spectrum[a].total_cmp(&spectrum[b]))\n' +
    '        .unwrap();\n' +
    '    let error = common::angular_error(angles[argmax].to_degrees(), &[40.0, 320.0]);\n' +
    '    assert!(error <= 0.5, "got {}°", angles[argmax].to_degrees());\n' +
    '}\n',
  '//! Helpers shared by the WAV-based integration tests.\n' +
    '\n' +
    '#![allow(dead_code)]\n' +
    '\n' +
    'use std::fs;\n' +
    'use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\n' +
    '\n' +
    'use nalgebra::DMatrix;\n' +
    '\n' +
    'pub const DATA_DIR: &str = "./tests/data/single-source";\n' +
    '\n' +
    '/// Ground truth encoded in a test-data filename.\n' +
    'pub struct Meta {\n' +
    '    pub frequency_hz: f64,\n' +
    '    pub doa_deg: f64,\n' +
    '    pub duration_s: f64,\n' +
    '}\n' +
    '\n' +

    '        .file_stem()\n' +
    '        .and_then(|s| s.to_str())\n' +
    '        .expect("bad file name");\n' +
    "    let parts: Vec<&str> = stem.split('_').collect();\n" +
    '    let num = |s: &str, suffix: &str| -> f64 { s.strip_suffix(suffix).unwrap().parse().unwrap() };\n' +
    '    Meta {\n' +

        } else {
            let step = angles[1] - angles[0];
            let mid = (a + b) as f64 / 2.0;
            if mid >= len as f64 {
                angles[0] + step * (mid - len as f64)
            } else {

    let r = runs.len();
    let mut peaks: Vec<(f64, f64)> = (0..r)

            let (a, b) = runs[k];
            let prev = match k {
                0 if circular => Some(score(runs[r - 1].1)),
                0 => None,
                _ => Some(score(runs[k - 1].1)),
            };
            let next = match k + 1 {
                j if j < r => Some(score(runs[j].0)),
                _ if circular => Some(score(runs[0].0)),

        })

input.code:
await $`git add src/music3d.rs src/music.rs src/lib.rs src/error.rs tests/music3d_test.rs tests/errors_test.rs tests/common/mod.rs`;
const msg = `Add MusicEstimator3d: narrowband DOA as azimuth and elevation

MusicEstimator3d takes [x, y, z] antenna positions and searches a regular
azimuth x elevation grid. Elevation is measured from the x-y plane, in
[-pi/2, pi/2]; the elevation grid holds the centres of equal cells, so the
poles (where every azimuth is the same direction) are never evaluated. It
reuses the 2-D covariance, noise subspace, steering (incl. Nyquist handling)
and scoring; with z = 0 and elevation 0 it gives the 2-D spectrum bit for bit.

Peaks are picked on the 2-D grid: azimuth wraps when the interval spans 2pi,
plateaus are reported at their centre, and towards the poles a point's
neighbours reach as many azimuth steps as span one elevation step, so that one
source does not show up as two peaks a few columns apart.

New error MusicError::InvalidElevationGrid for an empty grid or an interval
that is not finite, reversed, or reaches past the poles.

Tests use synthetic far-field plane waves (tests/common): tetrahedral and
octahedral arrays with 1-3 sources, noise, zenith/nadir, the azimuth seam,
shifted azimuth intervals, the planar mirror ambiguity, and the exact match
with the 2-D estimator on the recordings.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`;
await $`git commit -q -m ${msg}`;
await $`git log --oneline -4; git status --short`.text()
